question: Is MS protein-detection breadth predictable from gene properties? If yes, normal-tissue breadth contrasts (H1 in the ProteomicsDB audit: gated median 20 vs background 5 tissues, FALSIFIED toward gated MORE detected) may be detectability artifacts rather than biology.
universe: 196 study genes with mapped UniProt in results/proteomicsdb_per_gene.csv (205-gene study set; raw per-sample caches wiped - breadth outcome taken from the committed CSV)
features_note: the 7 locked propensity features; RNA abundance + tissue breadth proxy protein abundance, gene length proxies peptide count (protein sequences not available locally - named gap)
model: PoissonRegressor (log link, alpha=1.0), 5-fold CV (seed 20260929); CV deviance + pseudo-R2 reported; uninformative model (pseudo-R2 <= 0) reported as uninformative, not tuned
endpoints: CV fit quality of the detectability model

observed vs expected breadth per group: median observed and median expected n_normal_tissues for gated vs background; pre-declared reading: if the expected-group-gap explains >= 50% of the observed-group-gap direction, the H1 breadth contrast is substantially a detectability expectation artifact; if the observed gap exceeds expectation, residual real breadth difference remains
candidate antigens with the largest negative observed-minus-expected residuals (under-detected relative to properties -> normal breadth likely undercounted = safety-relevant list)
known_gaps: n=196 with 7 features is thin - point estimates reported with that caveat, no tuning; sequence-derived features (tryptic peptide count, hydrophobicity, protein length) unavailable locally - gene length is the proxy; breadth outcome is from the committed audit CSV, not recomputed from raw (wiped).
